messages.subject: How to upgrade bioconductor version within a packrat controlled project
messages.subject_clean: How to upgrade bioconductor version within a packrat controlled project
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Is there a correct procedure on upgrading the version of bioconductor in a packrat controlled project? For example, my R-3.1.0 installation is set to use Bioconductor version 2.14:

> library(BiocInstaller)
Bioconductor version 2.14 (BiocInstaller 1.14.2), ?biocLite for help

When I initialize the project to use packrat:

> packrat::init()
Initializing packrat project in directory:
- "/Users/fcchan/test"
--- Please select a CRAN mirror for use in this session ---

Adding these packages to packrat:
            _
    packrat   0.4.1-1

It sets up the packrat/packrat.snapshot as such:

PackratFormat: 1.4
PackratVersion: 0.4.1.1
RVersion: 3.1.0
Repos: CRAN=http://cran.stat.sfu.ca <http://cran.stat.sfu.ca>,
    BioCsoft=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/bioc <http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/bioc>,
    BioCann=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/annotation <http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/annotation>,
    BioCexp=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/experiment <http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/experiment>,
    BioCextra=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/extra <http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/extra>

Package: packrat
Source: CRAN
Version: 0.4.1-1
Hash: 5716097644904b9c1b4be2692de1600

This is all fine, but somewhere along the line I realized I need a particular version of a bioconductor package that was only available in Bioconductor 3.0. The R version 3.1.0 has the ability to support both the bioconductor version 2.14 and 3.0. As per the bioconductor manual, one can update the bioconductor like this:

source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite("BiocUpgrade") ## R version 2.15 or later

Bioconductor version 3.0 (BiocInstaller 1.16.0), ?biocLite for help

Packrat doesn't recognize a Bioconductor package upgrade:

>less packrat/packrat.lock

PackratFormat: 1.4
PackratVersion: 0.4.1.1
RVersion: 3.1.0
Repos: CRAN=http://cran.stat.sfu.ca <http://cran.stat.sfu.ca>,
    BioCsoft=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/bioc <http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/bioc>,
    BioCann=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/annotation <http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/annotation>,
    BioCexp=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/experiment <http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/experiment>,
    BioCextra=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/extra <http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/extra>

Package: BiocInstaller
Source: Bioconductor
Version: 1.16.0
Hash: a3c695ccdcf74d999deb8ddc86f8b7e8

Package: packrat
Source: CRAN
Version: 0.4.1-1
Hash: 5716097644904b9c1b4be2692de16005

In fact, the packrat snapshot mechanism fails since it still seeks the bioconductor packages found in the 2.14 repository. I tried to basically manually change the repositories to 3.0, but that came up some weird errors. Is there a proper way to do this?

Thanks,

messages.body_plain:
When snapshotting a project, packrat looks for the ‘active repositories’ — this is the union of whatever is in getOption('repos'), and the output for BiocInstaller::biocinstallRepos(). Can you confirm a couple things:
What is the output of BiocInstaller::biocinstallRepos()?
What is the output of getOption('repos')?

Performing:

> source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
> biocLite("BiocUpgrade")

> packrat::snapshot()

should be sufficient for updating the packrat project. Can you post the exact errors you’re receiving on packrat::snapshot()?
​

Hi,

So I did the following:

packrat::init()

source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite("BiocUpgrade")

packrat::snapshot()

When I run packrat::snapshot()

> packrat::snapshot()

The following packages are stale:
                  _
    BiocInstaller   1.16.0

These packages must be updated by calling packrat::restore() before
snapshotting. If you are sure you want the installed versions of these
packages to be snapshotted, call packrat::snapshot() again with
ignore.stale=TRUE.

I ran packrat::restore() and it says "Already up to date" and then ran packrat::snapshot() again with no messages. So it looks to be good. I close the R session. Restart the R session:

> library(BiocInstaller)

Bioconductor version 3.0 (BiocInstaller 1.16.0), ?biocLite for help

Warning message:
package ‘BiocInstaller’ was built under R version 3.1.1

I then proceed to install a package:

biocLite("TitanCNA")

This install no problem. Wait a bit and notice that the automatically snapshot mechanism fails. I then run packrat::snapshot()

> packrat::snapshot()

Adding these packages to packrat:

Error in getSourceForPkgRecord(pkgRecord, sourceDir, availablePkgs, repos) :

It seems to be that the S4Vectors fails because it is located in the Bioconductor 3.0 and not 2.14?

messages.body_plain:
Okay, I've reproduced this now and it looks like it's a bug in Packrat -- we're not respecting new repositories set as part of BiocInstaller. I'll generate a fix for this and commit to GitHub soon.

As a workaround, you can manually set the repositories:

    options(repos = c(getOption('repos')["CRAN"], BiocInstaller:::biocinstallRepos()))

That should help you resolve the problem in the meantime.

Den tisdagen den 23:e september 2014 kl. 20:10:45 UTC+2 skrev Kevin Ushey:
> Hi Paolo,
>
> Right now, packrat doesn't do anything particularly special with the version of R it records -- when you start a new R session, packrat will double-check its version against that in the stored project lockfile, and just provide a warning if it doesn't match. Otherwise, everything else will proceed as-is.
>
> The packrat private library is segmented in such a way that each version of R gets its own library, so you shouldn't have to worry about collisions there.
>
> Thanks,
> Kevin
>

messages.subject: Re: version control of unspecified files
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I see that packrat automatically adds packrat/src to .gitignore. src directory can grow large and I've been thinking about leaving it out and using `packrat::set_opts(local.repos = "<path_to_repo>")` to point packrat to all required sources. Is there a way to tell packrat not to modify .gitignore?

cheers,
Mateusz

On Monday, 29 September 2014 20:25:32 UTC+2, Kevin Ushey wrote:
> Hi Tim,
>
> All of the 'packrat/lib*' folders should normally be ignored (and packrat should add to the .gitignore automatically) Any other files within the packrat directory should typically be included in version control, although in some cases you might want to exclude package sources.
>
> It's highly advisable that you include `packrat.opts` and `packrat/init.R` under version control as well -- `packrat.opts` gives project-specific options that you would like to preserve over time, while `packrat/init.R` contains the logic that bounces an R session into packrat mode when R is launched in the project folder.
>
> Thanks,
> Kevin
>
> On Friday, September 26, 2014 6:34:33 AM UTC-7, Tim Bergsma wrote:
> > Hi.
> >
> > packrat help says add packrat/, packrat/src/, packrat/pacrat.lock to version control, but probably not packrat/lib/.
> >
> > What about packrat/init.R, packrat/lib-R, packrat/lib-ext, and packrat.opts?  I can guess, but it would be nice to have documented guidance.
> >
> > Thanks!
> >

messages.subject: Re: version control of unspecified files
messages.body_plain:
Found it
`vcs.ignore.src: TRUE` in packrat/packrat.opts.

cheers,
Mateusz
